findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: price_position, which_delivers, buyer_check, response_scan, plan_quote, dispute_pack · Private data: ping, price_position, which_delivers, spend_audit, response_scan, dispute_pack, registered_agent_card · Public sink: ping, price_position, which_delivers, response_scan, plan_quote, agent_payments_weekly · Destructive: proof_value, job_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: price_position, which_delivers, buyer_check, response_scan, plan_quote, dispute_pack · Private data: ping, price_position, which_delivers, spend_audit, response_scan, dispute_pack, registered_agent_card · Public sink: ping, price_position, which_delivers, response_scan, plan_quote, agent_payments_weekly · Destructive: proof_value, job_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_fair_offer" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
